title: A NASA Engineer Felt His Saliva Bubble In a Vacuum

scenes.text: A NASA engineer felt his own saliva bubble, and lived.
In the 1960s, Jim LeBlanc was testing a spacesuit inside a vacuum chamber.
Then his air hose came loose, and the pressure around him dropped to almost nothing in seconds.
He later said he felt the saliva on his tongue start to bubble just before he blacked out.
Studies of vacuum exposure say people lose consciousness in about ten seconds.
His coworkers got him out, and he recovered fully.

description:
NASA engineer Jim LeBlanc was testing a spacesuit in a vacuum chamber when his air hose disconnected.
He remembered the saliva on his tongue starting to bubble before he lost consciousness. Colleagues rescued him, and he recovered fully.
Would you test a spacesuit?
first_comment: What do you think you'd remember last if the air vanished around you?
